method_note: Read the whole target file. Picked claims by risk: repository metadata, release dates, specification versions and statuses, relation names and status codes that a linkset oracle would use, EU-law article citations, DOIs, the EUBOF/Battery Pass blockchain claim, and every existing_check mapping (compared against docs/reference/capabilities.md and src/dppce/adapters). Re-fetched primary sources with gh api, WebFetch, Crossref, Zenodo, local pdftotext on fetched PDFs. Protected EN/ISO/IEC/DIN documents were not opened. Claims about sibling records m02/m05/m06/m07 were not re-verified (out of scope).

checked.claim: IANA registry updated 2026-06-12; 'dpp' registered with a UNTP reference; 'linkset' (RFC 9264) registered; 'aas', 'aas-service-endpoints', 'dpp-service-endpoints' not registered.
checked.evidence: Page shows Last Updated 2026-06-12; dpp referenced to UN Transparency Protocol; linkset to RFC 9264; the three IDTA tokens are absent.

checked.claim: UNTP 0.7.0 is 'Pilots' (Maintained), Work in Progress 'Testing', 0.6.0 Unmaintained, no 1.0.
checked.evidence: Page lists exactly these three entries and no 1.0 (an 'all versions' link exists that was not followed).

checked.claim: GS1-Conformant Resolver Release 1.2.1 ratified August 2026; linkType=linkset or Accept linkset returns the linkset without redirect; malformed URI 400; unknown valid URI 404; otherwise redirect to default link.
checked.evidence: Page confirms 1.2.1, Aug 2026 (date shows a typo), 400 for failed validation, 404 for unknown valid URI, linkset not redirected, application/linkset+json per RFC 9264. The redirect status code for the default link is not specified by the standard.
checked.correction: Do not let an oracle assume 302 or 307 for the default-link redirect; the standard leaves the code open. Last 7148 characters of the page were not read.

checked.claim: IDTA ID Link: globalAssetId is the HTTP(S) ID Link; client sends Accept application/linkset+json (application/json lower priority); linkset relations aas, aas-service-endpoints, dpp, dpp-service-endpoints; linkset-unaware client may get 302 with Link rel=alternate type=application/linkset+json.
checked.evidence: All four relation tokens, the Accept pattern, 302 Found and the RFC 8288 Link header with rel alternate appear in the v3.2.0 page. The page says 'may' for 302, so it is not a requirement.

checked.claim: Linkset advertises operations GetAssetAdministrationShellVersionByIdAndDate, GetSubmodelVersionByIdAndDate (SSP-004), ReadDPPByProductId, ReadDPPVersionByProductIdAndDate with URL templates /dpps/... and /dppsByProductIdAndDate/...?date={date}; authentication hints use well_known_url and OAuth2.
checked.evidence: Every named operation, both URL templates, SSP-001/SSP-004 profile URIs, well_known_url and OAuth2 appear verbatim.

checked.claim: IDTA v3.2 example uses both 'dpp-service-endpoint' and 'dpp-service-endpoints'.
checked.evidence: The page text uses the singular in the ID Link example and the plural in the concept list. The '//' comment claim was not separately checked.

checked.evidence: Page says the service stores only the hash, names scope timestamp:write, shows Sep 30, 2026, and links to a reference at /api/core/timestamp. The submitter/block-number detail was not itemised in the fetch.

checked.claim: Regulation (EU) 2023/1542: passport from 18 February 2027 for LMT, industrial >2 kWh, EV (Art. 77(1)); QR links to unique identifier (77(3)); repurposing/remanufacturing gives linked passport (77(7)); ends after recycling (77(8)); identifier uploaded to registry (77(10)); Art. 78(a)-(h) topics.
checked.evidence: Consolidated text, chars 400000-500000: all paragraphs and the eight Art. 78 letters match the file's topics (interoperability, free access, storage, no resale, availability after exit, restricted write, integrity, security). Art. 77(2) tiers and 77(5) were not in the answer returned.

checked.evidence: Art. 13(6) requires a QR code on all batteries from 18 February 2027; for LMT, industrial >2 kWh and EV it links to the Art. 77 passport. Art. 13(7) covers placement.

checked.claim: Annex XIII point 4(c) lists battery status values original, repurposed, re-used, remanufactured, waste.
checked.evidence: Annex XIII point 4 (individual battery data for legitimate-interest holders) states the status options under 4(c).

checked.evidence: Matches. The four years run from entry into force of the Art. 13(5) implementing act.

checked.claim: 10.5281/zenodo.18711539 is a 2025 deliverable.
checked.evidence: Zenodo record gives title 'MaDiTraCe: D3.3 Guidelines for Methodology implementation', publication date 2026-02-20, type project deliverable.

checked.claim: Each paper's relevance statement (for example Made2Verify handles fallback when the manufacturer ceases operation; the 274 paper assigns governance to data spaces and identification to GS1).
checked.evidence: Crossref returns no abstract for the Procedia, ISSE and ACM records checked, so the content claims could not be compared with abstracts.
checked.correction: Mark relevance statements as based on search-tool snippets, not abstracts.

checked.claim: registry.consistency covers the mock registry 'backupURL only'.
checked.evidence: registry_consistency compares only identifier (registry vs passport id) and operator_identifier; no backup field exists in the check or the reference-server registry record, and nothing about backup appears in src or capabilities.md except persistence.scheduled (interface_only).
checked.correction: Existing check for the back-up objective: none. The mock registry record would need a back-up field and a new check (persistence.backup_equivalence already proposed).

checked.claim: Registry/carrier/resolver/back-up location consistency needs no new capability.
checked.evidence: registry.consistency compares registry identifier with the passport id and the operator identifier. It does not read the carrier identifier, the resolver target or any live/back-up location.
checked.correction: Only the identifier and operator-identifier part is covered today. Resolver-target and back-up location comparison need a new rule or check.

checked.claim: integrity.jws applies to the W3C VC-JOSE (vc+jwt) credential of the UNTP stack and 'returns not applicable' for a stack without integrity.
checked.evidence: The check finds the key only in an x5c header and returns INTEGRITY.KEY.UNSUPPORTED otherwise, so a kid/DID-URL vc+jwt cannot be verified. For an endpoint that does not return a compact JWS it returns INTEGRITY.TOKEN.MALFORMED (fail), not not_applicable; not_applicable comes from applicability, not from the check.
checked.correction: integrity.jws covers only x5c-based JWS. DID/kid vc+jwt needs a new capability (DID key resolution, offline). An unsigned passport is handled by applicability or manual/unsupported, not by this check.

checked.claim: api.contract can check operations advertised in a linkset against a pinned 'AAS Part 2 OpenAPI 3.2 subset'.
checked.evidence: Manifest: api.contract supports a subset of OpenAPI 3.1 (status, media type, JSON Schema); parameter table limits resource to item, model, signed, versions, registry_record and method to get. It cannot call arbitrary advertised hrefs or non-GET operations.
checked.correction: Existing check applies only to the five passport resources; linkset-driven operation checks are a new capability, and 'OpenAPI 3.2' should read OpenAPI 3.1 subset (3.2 is the AAS API version).

checked.claim: identifier.parse handles only GS1 Digital Link today; URN/DID/ID Link parsing is a new capability.
checked.evidence: parse() returns UNSUPPORTED (IDENTIFIER.SCHEME.UNSUPPORTED) for any scheme other than gs1-digital-link.

checked.claim: carrier.qr_decode (capability carrier.qr) and access.restricted_fields (capability access.policy) exist as named.
checked.evidence: Check-to-capability table lists both mappings; access.restricted_fields takes role (default anonymous).

rule5_findings.problem: Sentence reports that CX-0160 aligns field optionality with a protected DIN document. It only names the document and says it was not assessed, so it is low risk, but it paraphrases what a Catena-X text says about a DIN SPEC.
rule5_findings.fix: Reword to 'CX-0160 cites a DIN DKE SPEC; not assessed (fence)' with no reference to what the alignment covers.

rule5_findings.problem: Cites 'user stories chapter 6 headings' for e-signature/e-seal/eID/attestation, while scope_note and sources say chapters 4 and 6 were not used because they restate JTC 24 standards. The wording is in chapter 6 body text (and a chapter 5 figure). The content is eIDAS-based, not EN text, but the provenance statement is inconsistent with the stated fence.
rule5_findings.fix: State that the information comes from the chapter 5 figure and the registry onboarding user story, cite the user story section, and avoid describing any passage that attributes content to a JTC 24 standard.

rule5_findings.problem: Names the topics of protected documents ('two protected carrier/identifier standards', EN 18223, DIN DKE SPEC 99100) in the omitted-content notes. This is naming only and acceptable; no summary of their content was found anywhere in the file.
rule5_findings.fix: No change required. Keep the notes to numbers and titles.

missed_items.fact: The GS1-Conformant Resolver standard requires redirection to the default link but does not fix the HTTP status code, so an oracle must accept any redirect status the ICS declares.
The 24 November 2026 date belongs to Use Case 2 (CX-0160-2) going live with CX-Neptune, added through a fast-track process; the base standard is itself not yet certifiable.

Art. 13(1) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 sets 19 July 2026 for the Commission to set up the digital registry; relevant to the registry layer because the date has passed at retrieval, yet registry.official stays interface_only.
integrity.jws locates the key only in an x5c header, so UNTP-style vc+jwt with a DID-URL kid is outside current capability; this belongs in the L08 gap list.
BatteryPass-Ready sources disagree on partner numbers (over 100 on the project page, 67 logos shown, over 80 in a GS1 Germany partner news item).
RFC 9264 gives every link context an optional anchor and recommends explicit anchors; an anchor-equality oracle should treat a missing anchor as 'not stated', not as a mismatch.

overall: The file is reliable on external facts: repository metadata, release dates, IANA and UNTP statuses, IDTA relation names and operation names, CX-0160 content, EU-law article citations and the Battery Pass / EUBOF blockchain finding all matched primary sources, and the EUBOF claim was confirmed from the report text. The two weak areas are the literature block (one wrong year for the Zenodo record; relevance statements not checkable against abstracts) and the existing_check mappings, where four entries overstate what the engine does: registry.consistency has no back-up field, integrity.jws cannot verify kid-based vc+jwt and does not return not-applicable, and api.contract cannot follow linkset-advertised operations. No rule 5 violation was found; one provenance inconsistency about user-story chapter 6 should be fixed. Sibling-record claims (m02, m05, m06, m07) were not re-verified.
